thread.title: Apple Loses Support But Dow At High; Bitcoin Play Goes Positive

author: NANCY GONDO
title: Apple Loses Support But Dow At High; Bitcoin Play Goes Positive
text:
The Dow Jones industrial average marched to a new record despite another drop by Apple ( AAPL ). Bitcoin trimmed its deficit.
X SPDR Dow Jones Industrial Average ( DIA ) held a 0.6% gain, while PowerShares QQQ Trust ( QQQ ) advanced 0.3% and SPDR S&P 500 ( SPY ) climbed 0.2%.
3M ( MMM ), Boeing ( BA ) and United Technologies ( UTX ) led the blue chip index with respective gains of 2.3%, 2.4% and 1.6%. Apple extended its loss to 1.2% to breach its 50-day moving average. It's so far been unable to gain momentum after re-clearing a 176.34 buy point last week, and is back below the entry. Morgan Stanley lowered its price target on the iPhone maker to $200 from $205.
Biotech, health care and utilities were among sector funds advancing in the stock market today . Oil plays were mixed as West Texas intermediate crude prices rose 0.4% to $65.90 a barrel. Gold ETFs were also mixed; gold futures were slightly higher.
Homebuilders, real estate and chips lagged. VanEck Vectors Semiconductor ( SMH ) reversed to a 0.8% loss. Lam Research ( LRCX ) surged early after reporting better-than-expected quarterly results late Wednesday, but reversed sharply lower. Its relative strength line has been lagging its stock price action. But graphics chip designer Nvidia ( NVDA ) advanced 1% and is just off its Tuesday high.
Bitcoin also underperformed, though its price has held relatively steady this week. The digital currency was down 1.3% to $11,256.17, according to CoinDesk , after rising to $11,711.00 earlier. Bitcoin Investment Trust ( GBTC ), however, staged an upside reversal and edged 1% higher. It continues to hit upward resistance at its 50-day moving average.
Brazil Rising? A pair of Brazil ETFs are trading at their best levels in more than three years as the Ibovespa index soars to record highs.
The Sao Paulo stock exchange leapt nearly 4% Wednesday, after a Brazilian appeals court upheld a graft conviction against ex-President Luiz Inacio Lula de Silva. That's likely to hurt his chances of running for president in October.
IShares MSCI Brazil Capped ( EWZ ) surged 6% to its highest level since October 2014. The fund closed near the top of a buy range that started at a 44.12 buy point . It advanced nearly 9% from an early-September (2017) breakout to an Oct. 5 intraday high.
The ETF, which tracks the MSCI Brazil 25/50 Index, has gathered $8.3 billion since its July 2000 launch. It was last featured in this ETF column on Sept. 8, as shares rose to their highest price since November 2014. Brazil has had its share of political scandals. In May, EWZ plunged 16% amid reports President Michel Temer was involved in a corruption scandal.
It's come a long way since. Financials accounted for nearly 38% of assets as of Jan. 23, followed by about 15% apiece in materials and consumer staples. Energy contributed 8% and industrials 6%. Top holdings included banks Itau Unibanco ( ITUB ) and Banco Bradesco ( BBD ), mining company Vale, beer producer Ambev ( ABEV ), and regional exchange Brasil Bolsa Balcao. The top five made up 43% of the 55-stock portfolio.
